meta.title: Inside a neural interface · {brand}
meta.description: An illustrative view of a microelectrode array in motor cortex, with firing replayed from an open monkey recording and a precomputed decoder moving a cursor and a simulated arm. Research demo; not a medical device; no hardware is controlled.

hero.heading: Inside a neural interface
hero.lede: Follow a signal from neurons in the motor cortex, up an implanted electrode array and its lead, into a decoder, and out as movement. The anatomy and the device are drawings; the firing is replayed from a real, openly published monkey recording.

banner: Illustrative anatomy and device; not a specific product. Firing replayed from open data. Not a medical device. Offline replay; no hardware is controlled.
sceneLabel: Interactive three-dimensional scene of an illustrative electrode array in motor cortex. Use the controls below the scene to play, take the guided tour, show or hide layers and inspect an electrode.

fallback.alt: Still image of the interactive scene: a translucent block of motor cortex with a grid electrode array inserted, glowing neurons near the electrode tips, a lead to a headstage, a decoder, a cursor screen and a simulated arm.

fallback.caption: A still frame of the scene. The anatomy and the device are drawings; the firing shown is replayed from the open recording.

controls.heading: Scene controls
controls.orbitHint: Drag to orbit, scroll or pinch to zoom, click a shank to inspect it. With the keyboard: focus the scene, then use the arrow keys to orbit, plus and minus to zoom and Home to reset; the electrode list inspects a shank.

tour.overview: An illustrative block of motor cortex, cut open, with a grid electrode array on its surface.
tour.array: Each shank of the array ends in a recording tip in the cortex. The grid layout of channels here is a drawing convention.
tour.neurons: Neurons near the tips glow when they fire. The spike times are replayed from the open recording.
tour.signal: Each spike travels up its shank and the lead to a headstage, which digitises it.
tour.decoder: Every fifty milliseconds the counts go to a decoder, whose estimate moves the cursor and the simulated arm.

inspect.heading: Electrode detail
inspect.empty: Click a shank in the scene, or choose an electrode above, to see its activity.
inspect.traceNote: The open file holds spike times, not raw voltage. The trace is drawn: its spikes sit at the real spike times, but the waveform shape and background noise are illustrative.
inspect.noUnits: No sorted units were recorded on this electrode.

notes.heading: What is real here, and what is drawn
items: Real: the spike times of every neuron, the reaches and the decoded path. They are the same held-out test reaches and ridge-filter output shown on the Neural Playground.
Drawn: the tissue, the array, the lead, the headstage and the arm. They are illustrative and do not depict a specific product or implant.
Drawn: where each recorded neuron sits. The file names the electrode each neuron was recorded on, but not the physical layout of the array.
Replay runs at half speed so single spikes stay visible. Nothing is decoded in real time, and no hardware is controlled.

Derived from MC_RTT (CC BY 4.0); changes were made: we excerpted twelve held-out reaches, counted spikes in fifty-millisecond bins and replay them at half speed; the moving cursor and arm follow a linear decoder's output, with positions rounded to a tenth of a millimetre. The dataset's creators do not endorse {brand}.
